title: Replace repeated whole-prefix work with a monotonic incremental state machine

source.title: vLLM PR #55565 incremental DeepSeek V3/V3.1 delimiter state, extending PR #40298 review evidence
source.claim_scope: The open source reports differential parser equivalence and parser-loop speedups for two DeepSeek parsers; it is not maintainer approval, independent reproduction, server latency or target-hardware proof.

implementation_recipe: Write a transition table for request start, first cumulative compatibility check, incremental updates, item completion and request completion.
Derive the smallest sufficient prefix summary: use counters or flags when a full grammar cursor and suffix buffer are unnecessary.
Perform at most one cumulative scan, then process each new delta once and advance externally visible indices exactly once at the owning transition.
Keep semantic reconstruction on the trusted batch or existing streaming path so the optimization does not invent a second serialization contract.
Bind state lifetime to one coherent request stream and make reset, reuse and interleaving behavior explicit.
validation_recipe: Compare normalized incremental output with the frozen baseline or batch oracle over every single split point and deterministic random chunk partitions.
Cover no-item, one-item, multiple-item, incomplete input, surrounding text, empty chunks, delimiter fragments and parser reuse.
Instrument cumulative containers so tests fail if steady-state updates perform membership, count, slice or search on accepted history.
Measure complete production-boundary work over increasing history lengths and multiple delta sizes, then check whether total work changes from quadratic toward linear.
Separate the common no-item path from the actual-item path and reject a claimed universal speedup when their intervals differ or overlap.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Repeated whole-history scanning should become near-linear total work in emitted input length.
Delimiter recognition, tokenizer, allocation, logging and output serialization can become dominant after old-prefix work is removed.
State ownership and transition correctness replace raw scan cost as the primary risk.
failure_modes: A transition clears unconsumed suffix data that belongs to the next field or normal-text state.
State is reset too early, survives across requests or is shared by interleaved streams.
A delimiter split across chunks is emitted, skipped or recognized twice.
The first observed delta starts after a marker already present in cumulative history and an over-aggressive delta-only fast path misses it.
Cached counts diverge when another code path mutates accepted history or changes delimiter identity.
The implementation retains complete history under a new state object and preserves quadratic slicing or search work.
A no-item microbenchmark is generalized to actual structured-output responses without separate evidence.
scope_limits: Use only when successive calls reconsider a shared growing prefix and state can be owned for the same semantic stream.
Do not transfer concrete delimiters, field names, reset rules or malformed-input behavior across parser protocols.
PR #40298 is closed-unmerged and PR #55565 remains open; both remain discovery evidence rather than merge endorsement.
The later source reports CPU parser-loop measurements, not server latency, GPU throughput or target-workload materiality.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: Call k reprocesses history 0..k even though call k-1 already established a valid summary of 0..k-1.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: successive input deltas within one request-local stream
local_state: monotonic consumed cursor or first-scan flag
bounded unresolved delimiter suffix when required
cached prefix flags or delimiter counts
current grammar state and externally visible item index
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Update the smallest sufficient prefix summary from prior state and only the new delta, retaining only unresolved grammar context.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Emit newly completed semantic fields, preserve trailing unconsumed input, and reset only at the explicit request boundary.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Target O(total input plus emitted output) over the stream instead of O(number of deltas times accumulated history).
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: Each call depends on bounded parser state and its new delta, except for one explicitly bounded compatibility scan.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: Adds request-local state reads and writes while removing repeated reads of historical tokens or text.
invariants: concatenated incremental output equals the trusted complete-input semantic result
every accepted input unit is summarized once except a bounded compatibility scan or delimiter suffix
indices and cumulative counts advance exactly once at their owning transition
state lifetime is exactly one coherent request stream
anti_patterns: append to a full-history buffer and search it again
use delta-only detection before establishing compatibility with cumulative history
test only delimiter-aligned chunks or only the no-item path
duplicate the batch parser's type and serialization rules
reset all state inside a per-item completion transition

candidate_archetypes.name: bounded-suffix incremental parser
candidate_archetypes.template: Track consumed position and grammar state, process only each new delta, and retain only the bounded suffix needed to resolve a split delimiter.

candidate_archetypes.name: cached prefix summary
candidate_archetypes.template: Cache the smallest sufficient flags or counters for the accepted prefix, perform one compatibility scan when needed, and update only from each delta under an explicit stream epoch.
